scores.evidence: Phase 1 Prototype: "Ingestion, hybrid search, generation with citations, first evaluation scores"
scores.rationale: Broad order is sensible (discovery, prototype, internal, beta), but guardrails and handoff come in Phase 3 after generation, and evaluation is said to come first yet lands with the prototype.

scores.evidence: Phase 0 is "Discovery": "Doc inventory, ticket analysis, metrics agreed, test set started"
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is only discovery, and the first build is a prototype with no stated production path; agent assist is a real but later slice.

scores.evidence: "I don't know your stack... uses common defaults and marks the choices that depend on your answers."
scores.rationale: Open questions and stack options are listed, but there are no default-plus-flip-condition decisions, except for the model choice and the agent-assist-first recommendation.
Nothing orders work within phases by blast radius; the sections are listed by topic.

scores.evidence: "Prompt injection: Clean up ingested content, keep system instructions separate from retrieved text, and give the bot no ability to act on accounts in v1."
scores.rationale: Security has a solid dedicated section, but it is not tied to phases, and the guardrails only ship in Phase 3.

scores.evidence: "Dashboards for the metrics in §1, plus alerts on spikes in handoffs or errors."
scores.rationale: Observability is well described, but it is a standalone section; dashboards are listed only in Phase 3, not in Phases 0 or 1.
The plan says nothing about reproducible builds, environments, index rebuilds or data versioning; CI regression tests are the nearest thing.

scores.evidence: "Remove deleted or unpublished articles from the index right away"; "Confidence check: ... hand off to a human."
scores.rationale: Failure handling such as handoff, confidence fallback and rate limits is described, but not phase by phase, and it has no retries, timeouts or provider-outage handling.

scores.evidence: "Treat retrieved text as data, not instructions"; "token budgets"; "Handoff to a human"; Phase 3: "handoff working, guardrails"
scores.rationale: Retrieval, generation, guardrails, handoff and feedback are all covered, but the defenses, budgets and human-in-the-loop are built after retrieval and generation, and model access, memory and routing are not sequenced.

scores.evidence: "5. Later — Logged-in account actions via tool calls (order status, plan details), more languages, voice/email channels"
scores.rationale: Out-of-scope items and a Later phase are listed, but none has a pull-forward condition.

note: A sound, practical RAG design with good content on evaluation, retrieval and security, but it is organised by topic and not by dependency order. It lacks a production walking skeleton, decision gates with flip conditions, reproducibility, and security or observability tied to each phase.
